h1: Patios and hardscaping in Longview & East Texas
lede: Paver and flagstone patios, walkways, fire pits and seating walls, dug out and built on a compacted base so they stay level in East Texas clay. Most projects run $3,100 to $9,100.
answer: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned, fully insured hardscaping company in Longview, TX, building across East Texas since 2017 with a 5.0 rating across {{REVIEWS}} Google reviews. We build paver and flagstone patios, walkways, fire pits, seating walls and outdoor kitchens on a dug-out, compacted base, pitched so water runs away from the house. Most projects run $3,100 to $9,100, set by square footage, material and how the site sits. Request a free walkthrough and written estimate online.
overview: A patio is only as good as what's under it. We dig to the right depth, lay and compact a real base, and pitch the surface so water runs away from the foundation, not toward it. Our clay swells when it's wet and shrinks when it dries, and a patio set on loose fill can look great in May and sink by August.

We build with concrete pavers, flagstone and chopped stone. Recent work includes a flagstone walkway in Kilgore with chopped stone borders and path lighting, a checkerboard paver patio with gravel joints off a covered porch, also in Kilgore, and a 475 square foot Cherokee flagstone patio in White Oak built around a chopped stone fire pit, with one corner raised on a chopped stone wall.
included: Flagstone patios, paths and stepping stones

process.title: Walk the site
process.text: We look at the slope, where water runs, how the space connects to the house, and how we'll get material in.

process.title: Plan and price it
process.text: You get a written, itemized estimate with the material, size and base spec. If you want to see it first, the $449 Hardscape Preview gives you layout renderings.

price.note: A small patio or walkway lands at the low end, and a large outdoor living build costs more. You get the exact number in a written, itemized estimate after we walk the site.
factors: How much excavation and base the site needs

timing: We build patios year-round in East Texas, and spring and fall book up first. Base work goes best in a dry stretch, because saturated clay won't compact. If you want to be sitting on it by a certain season, call a few weeks ahead.

east_texas.title: What sinks patios in East Texas
text: Most patio failures here come from the dirt, not the stone. Much of this area is sandy loam over red clay, and the clay moves. It swells after heavy spring rain and shrinks in a dry August. A patio laid on a thin bed of sand over that will settle, rock and split.

So we dig out to the right depth, compact a crushed stone base, and pitch the surface away from the house. Where a patio sits at the bottom of a slope or catches roof water, we plan the drainage before we set the first paver, because water getting under a patio is what undermines it.

faq.q: How much does a paver patio cost in Longview, TX?
faq.a: Most patio and hardscape projects run $3,100 to $9,100. A small patio or walkway costs less, and a large outdoor living build with walls, a fire pit or a kitchen costs more. Square footage, the material you pick, and how much grading and base work the site needs drive the number. We walk it for free and send a written, itemized estimate.

faq.q: What kind of hardscaping do you build?
faq.a: Paver and flagstone patios, walkways and stepping-stone paths, fire pits and outdoor fireplaces, seating walls, retaining walls, and outdoor kitchens with grill stations. Recent jobs include a flagstone walkway with path lighting and a checkerboard paver patio in Kilgore, and a Cherokee flagstone patio around a chopped stone fire pit in White Oak.

faq.q: How long does a patio take to build?
faq.a: Most residential patios and walkways take a few days to a couple of weeks. Size matters, but so does the ground. A site that needs grading or drainage work takes longer than a flat, open backyard, and a long wet stretch can push the dig back. You get a timeline in your written estimate before we start.

faq.q: How do you keep a patio from sinking in East Texas clay?
faq.a: By building the base right. We dig out to the proper depth, compact a real base, and pitch the surface so water runs away from the house. Clay that gets wet under a patio swells and then shrinks as it dries, and that movement is what sinks and cracks a patio. Drainage gets planned before we set the first piece.

faq.q: Can I see a design before you build?
faq.a: Yes. The $449 Hardscape Preview gives you layout renderings from the top and in perspective, a material spec, dimensions, base-prep notes, and drainage and pitch notes, with one round of revisions. It covers patios, walkways, walls and fire pits. The fee is credited toward a qualifying install booked within 90 days.
